arma_tracker.title: American Reserve Modernization Act progress
arma_tracker.status: Introduced · referred to House Financial Services
arma_tracker.summary: Would put a Treasury-administered Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into statute, establish long-term holding requirements and require public proof-of-reserve reporting. This is proposed legislation, not an enacted law or a Federal Reserve purchase announcement.
arma_tracker.impact: Potentially supportive for Bitcoin if enacted: more durable custody and retention rules. It does not itself demonstrate new purchases or guarantee price gains.
arma_tracker.next_step: Watch for House Financial Services committee action, followed by House passage. Both chambers must agree on the same text before enactment; the stages are milestones, not a probability or timetable.
arma_tracker.verification_note: Introduction and referral verified against the official GovInfo bill record. No later milestone verified. Congress.gov's live action feed could not be accessed during this check; pending means not verified complete in this dated snapshot, not a live legislative feed.

central_banks.summary: A US$1 million digital-asset test portfolio includes Bitcoin, stablecoins and a tokenized deposit. The bank plans a two-to-three-year evaluation.
The ECB's May 2025 Financial Stability Review records the ECB President's position that Bitcoin would not enter General Council central-bank reserves.

events.headline: Czech central bank proposes Bitcoin portfolio analysis
events.change: The governor proposed formally studying a Bitcoin test portfolio.
events.why: Official study is an early adoption signal, but it is neither approval nor a purchase.

events.headline: United States establishes Strategic Bitcoin Reserve policy
events.change: The executive order directed Treasury to administer qualifying forfeited government Bitcoin as reserve assets and generally not sell it.
events.why: It changes federal policy from disposal toward strategic retention, while additional acquisition must be budget neutral.

events.headline: House passes H.R. 3633
events.change: The bill cleared the House and moved to the Senate.
events.why: Progress toward a federal market-structure framework may reduce regulatory uncertainty, but the bill was not yet law.

events.headline: White House report confirms Treasury operating direction
events.change: The report says Treasury will administer the reserve and continue coordinating on operational next steps.
events.why: It confirms policy continuity, but does not publish a fully reconciled Bitcoin balance or announce open-market purchases.

events.headline: Czech National Bank launches digital-asset pilot
events.change: The bank purchased a small test portfolio containing Bitcoin outside its international reserves.
events.why: It is verified operational adoption by a central bank, but not a reserve allocation.

events.headline: Senate Banking advances CLARITY Act 15–9
events.change: The Senate Banking Committee advanced H.R. 3633 in a bipartisan vote.
events.why: The bill moved closer to floor consideration but still had no force of law.

events.headline: Senate-reported version published
events.change: GovInfo lists the bill as reported in the Senate with an amendment.
events.why: This is the latest formal congressional status in the official bill record used here; reported does not mean enacted.

events.headline: Updated merged Senate text released
events.change: Senator Lummis released text combining Banking and Agriculture committee work.
events.why: Updated text signals active negotiation, but it is not a floor vote or enactment.

methodology: Only dated primary-government or central-bank statements are treated as verified events. Status describes legal or operational progress; impact is a separate directional interpretation for Bitcoin. Supportive does not mean the event guarantees a higher Bitcoin price. Proposals, studies and pilots are not counted as official reserve allocations.
